mentl/7a6dc2b:
Exploratory changes trying to get the WASM bootstrap to successfully
compile a user program. None of these on their own fix the underlying
issue, but they narrow the failure mode and make debugging easier.

- emit_module: bump initial memory from 256 pages (16 MB) to 32768 pages
  (2 GB). This eliminates memory.grow as a confounding variable — the
  bootstrap now has 2 GB of headroom without any grow calls. The crash
  STILL happens, at address 0xdc02bd35 (3.7 GB). This rules out grow
  failure as the root cause.

- emit_module: vstack expands from 4 KB (1024 slots) to 1 MB (256K slots).
  Deeply nested expressions in the self-hosted compiler push a lot onto
  __vsp; 1024 slots was insufficient and overflow silently corrupts the
  heap. Bigger vstack eliminates that category of bug.

- emit_alloc: sanity trap on allocation > 16 MB (previously 1 MB, which
  was too aggressive and tripped on read_file's legit 128 KB buffer).
  Trap on memory.grow failure (previously silently dropped the return).

- emit_global_decls: bail explicitly if a global name's length > 100
  (identifier corruption) with ";; CORRUPT GLOBAL NAME" marker so a
  debugger can distinguish "corrupted pointer" from "legit huge alloc".

Current state of the bootstrap self-compile:
- Compiles cleanly (127K lines of valid WAT)
- wasmtime compiles without error
- At runtime on input `let x = 42`: crashes in emit_global_decls at
  recursion depth ~19 with a memory fault at a deterministic address
  ending in bytes "02 b? XX" (pattern across runs: 02bfaa, 02bfac,
  02bd35). This looks like a corrupted pointer being dereferenced,
  not OOM.

The pattern across crash addresses strongly suggests a specific
structure's field is being read as a pointer — probably a variant
tag or list header with garbage in those bytes. Next investigator
should dump memory around the crash site or instrument emit_global_decls
to print the first few global name pointers before the recursion begins.

landed/7ae55a5:
Assemble, gate, submit, track: one transaction at a time through four
timed stages, returning what happened and where the milliseconds went.

Gates run on evidence gathered from live chain state, and an I/O failure
while gathering it rejects the transaction instead of skipping the check.
ComputeCeiling rejects when the node reports no consumption at all;
unknown is not safe.

Talks JSON-RPC directly rather than depending on solana-client, which
drags the full RPC stack in to submit one transaction and whose stable
4.x release resolves solana-transaction-status-client-types against
wincode 0.5 while solana-sdk's types implement wincode 0.6, so the two
do not compile together.

CI runs the pipeline against a real solana-test-validator on every push.
That caught the first bug before it shipped: Message::new leaves the
blockhash zeroed, so getFeeForMessage priced an invalid message and
returned null, and every gate correctly failed closed.

The Jito client is a clean port of the one in flowpilot, the trading
engine this is extracted from.
